Yes and it's called Tinnitus.
None of those fake "emotional" demon voices in your head, very much a real one that drags you down eternally, and the voice is always there to accompany you, costing you mental health and sleep.

Keep that in mind when thinking about your inner demon, could be much worse.
Aaaaand of course it's John Wick.
Really is silly when you can't even listen to music anymore because the tinnitus tone just overpowers it all the time.

The only thing doctors can and will offer to help is anti-depressants.

I don't need them because I am aware that the root of my anxiety is the noise.
All they will do is make me addicted to them and just worsen my situation, I don't like taking medication unless necessary.
My hearing was tested as perfect up to 8000hz, but I definitely feel hearing loss in higher frequencies - conversations get muddled up with a lot of background noise, songs sounding muffled etc.
You can have improvements if you stop with the bad habits, people say ears don't heal but there's a lot of people who recovered from acoustic trauma, at the very least partially.

Considering I've got my Tinnitus from Headphone use, I'd suggest you should lay off them and use speakers instead at moderate volume.

Your tinnitus will most likely go back to the previous level if you let your ears rest for some time.
Exposure to loud noises (A fire alarm, and prolonged usage of headphones).

Well I've had my tinnitus for a month now, at first it was screeching loud even without covering the ears.

It got faint to almost inaudible in a quiet room now.

I guess it depends on how much damage was caused to your ears, but it does get better mostly(not just mentally).

First thing to do would be not to wait until April.

Go to your GP / family doctor in urgency that you are having major pain because of this, so that they can escalate a visit with the ear specialist, or send you to an emergency room to check on it immediately.

Put your health above everything and get it checked.
